coverageSpotVerification.detail: Every sampled mapping exercises its assertion’s observable with real data, and several exceed it: m8-a01 recomputes the six lifetime totals from raw audit table scans rather than from a seeded constant, and m6-a13 replays all fifty sample actions and then verifies roster, message counts, quote, reactions, media, the view-once flag and post counts. No stub, tautological, or misdirected mapping was found. Three mappings are weak but not dishonest, each covering the item’s main clause while leaving a parenthetical clause unexercised: m2-a22 (asserts ">20 items after scrolling" but not the "20 per page" clause, and the Following feed in fact pages at 10), m5-a09 (queries only the lowercase term, so the case-insensitivity clause is unexercised, and the documented API is in fact case-sensitive), and m8-a05 (its two in-window posts have equal like counts, so it tests the tie-break rather than "most likes first"; independent execution with unequal counts passes). Independently, all 41 records in the seven latest per-segment choreography JSONL files validate against the frozen receipts.schema.json.

defects.summary: Identically-retried media mutations leak a staged asset copy that is never attached and never released; a handful of retries exhausts first the per-principal and then the OWNER-WIDE staging ceiling, after which every media upload on the instance fails for every account. Not cleared by a backend restart. This is what terminated the lane’s M1/M2/M5/M6.
defects.evidence: grading/evidence/g9-viewonce-staging.json (12 distinct view-once sends commit; the same send retried with an identical id fails on retry 7 with "E_ASSET_TOO_LARGE: the owner has reached the 536870912 byte or 40 object staging ceiling", after which ordinary sendMedia also fails while text send still commits); grading/evidence/g8-staging-and-seed.json (26 distinct uploads are fine, so the leak is retry-specific); snapback/messages.q:41 "if exists messages[id]: return { id }" and :153 "if exists intents[viewer, mutationId]: return true", both of which discard the already-staged upload; lib/sendViewOnce.mjs re-uploads once per conversation member; evidence/m6-suite-1788636726916.json for the lane’s own occurrence; trace.md#the-staged-asset-leak-defect-d-01

O1.anchorsCited: O1 anchors: "30: core features partially work; several checklist items fail" / "60: M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap" / "90: every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts". Placed between the 30 and 60 anchors, nearer 30.
O1.justification: Full scope, so all eight milestones are in the denominator, and applicability.json’s O1 rule scores every non-green milestone’s checklist as not passed. Statuses: M3, M4 and M8 green; M1, M2, M5 and M6 aborted; M7 not-run. That credits 45 of the 119 enumerated assertions (37.8%). The 60 anchor is out of reach because M1 and M2 - the foundation - are not credited, M7 was never attempted, and the M6/M8 native platform-proof artifacts were never produced (run record native.proof false for both). It sits above the 30 anchor because the implementation underneath is strong: on independent grader execution 97 of 119 assertions pass, the M1/M2/M4/M5 suites all pass against a restarted backend, the three credited milestones include the additive M8 in full, and the aborts trace to one resource-leak defect (d-01) plus one edit-loss race (d-02) rather than to unbuilt features.

O2.anchorsCited: O2 anchors: "30: multiple high-severity defects in core flows" / "60: a few medium defects off the happy path" / "90: only cosmetic nits". Placed at the 30 anchor.
O2.justification: Two high-severity defects sit squarely in core flows. d-01 (blocker) is an unbounded staged-asset leak reachable through the retry contract API.md itself documents; seven identical view-once retries took a fresh instance from healthy to "no account can upload any media", and a backend restart did not clear it - it is the direct cause of the lane’s own M1/M2/M5/M6 aborts. d-02 (major) is silent data loss in profile editing: typed edits are discarded and stale values written back with no error. Four further minor defects (d-03 page size, d-04 case-sensitive documented search, d-05 documented page size vs behaviour, d-06 probe methodology), one more minor hygiene item (d-09) and two cosmetic ones (d-07 raw refusal envelopes in the UI, d-08 an uncaught page error) sit below them. That is the 30 anchor almost verbatim; it is not pushed lower because trust boundaries held under every spot check (foreign-conversation reads denied, non-member sends rejected, non-admin mutations rejected, post-logout tokens revoked, post-delete and post-view assets refused including unauthenticated).

O5.bandRationale: First-match order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. Band 0 does not fire: the third replay attempt passed with 167,244 settled receipts (unique keys, all committed, matching the expected total) and 3,258 end-state checks with zero failures, and the verifier does cover the named O5 fixtures - u0500’s 500 follows and 100 conversations, u0005’s 5 follows, celebrity u0900’s 900 followers and 200 posts, u0901’s exact 5-account following list, and g0001’s 50-member roster and 10,000 messages - so the invariant manifest conforms; and the replay used 3,881 s of its 14,400 s cap (27.0%), so the cap was not exhausted. Band 30 fires on a degradation-rule failure: "Following-feed load for the 500-follow probe user <= 3x the same query for a 5-follow user" fails at every checkpoint - 303.4 ms vs 18.6 ms (16.3x) at 10%, 619.2 ms vs 15.6 ms (39.7x) at 50%, and 951.8 ms vs 19.7 ms (48.3x) at the full corpus - and it fails on medians too (22x / 42x / 47x), so it is not a tail artifact. No probe timed out, errored or OOMed, and the two M8 rules that are measured pass (Insights 6.42 -> 3.69 -> 4.35 ms, Trending 10.78 -> 10.78 -> 15.38 ms, both within 3x with the mid-curve point under the line). Evidence: evidence/scale-3-result.json, scale-3-full-verification.json, scale-3-{10%,50%,full}-probes.json. Note that the probes themselves deviate from the frozen methodology (defect d-06), but the failing ratio is far outside any sampling artifact.

notes: DEVIATIONS (this run is N=1 calibration, not a claim-eligible wave). (1) No holdout probe set was committed for this wave: execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the literal none-uncommitted, probeResults is empty, and no probes were invented. O3 would in any case have been null on its own predicate. (2) The claude family has not passed the grader calibration gate, so calibrationPassed is false and the grade is labelled uncalibrated-grader. sameFamilyGraded is false. (3) PORT SUBSTITUTION. The lane documents 49100-49103 but 49100-49102 on this machine belong to an unrelated program (lsof: cwd .../clique-improvement/grading/astra-006/app). The lane ran on 49120 (backend), 49121 (web client) and 49122 (push seam). No lane file on disk was edited; the substitution was applied by a Node module load hook that rewrites the literal loopback ports in modules under scripts/, lib/, tools/ and snapback/ at load time, plus EXPO_PUBLIC_SNAPBACK_URL for the web client. Grader-generated artifacts were redirected into grading/evidence/; the backend-owned idempotency journals (evidence/seed-*.jsonl, evidence/sample-50-receipts.jsonl) were deliberately not redirected and were byte-identical before and after. (4) THE PUSH SEAM COULD NOT BE POINTED AT THE SUBSTITUTED PORT. snapback/provider.ts and snapback/digestProvider.ts pin http://127.0.0.1:49102 in the effect grants, and the effect source is compiled into the generated .snapback/build/project.json executed by the native dev binary, which the module hook does not reach. Letting the effect fire would have POSTed this lane payloads into the unrelated program push server and polluted its evidence, so presence.replayMode({enabled:true}) was set for the whole session. This blocked independent execution of exactly m6-a08, m6-a09, m8-a08, m8-a09, m8-a10 and m8-a11, which are graded from the lane own receipts and flagged in their notes. m8-a12 was verified independently by another route. (5) Timing-sensitive checks are best-of-3 per the frozen prompt; machine load (uptime) was recorded beside every timed step in grading/evidence/uptime-*.txt. The machine was heavily shared throughout (load average 9-22). (6) SCHEMA LIMIT. This grader-report schema predates the M8 amendment: assertionResults is additionalProperties:false over ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$, so M8 assertion ids cannot be keyed there without making the report invalid. The eighteen M8 results are therefore recorded here and in trace.md, and they are included in the O1 judgement.
